title: The Ascent (1977) is a fantastic WWII film, and now one of my favorites WWII films!

commenti.body:
The Ascent routinely gets in my all time top 5 list.

The 1st half is just astounding action cinema, it would be as effective if it was completely silent. The rest of the film is also brilliant but entirely different. A real philosophical and moral drama. 

Well worth watching.

*The Ascent* is incredible and connected to *Come and See*  in that the female director was the wife of the director of *Come and See*.

The themes of resistance for resistance sake are beautiful. He who resists being compared to Christ in the end. These themes were popular during WW2, but seem more and more out of Vogue of late. It's hard for us to imagine being trapped in a situation where an honorable death is better than an inevitable one running or hiding.

Spoiler: I'm a milsurp gun collector and watching the mosin suicide attempt is something I never even considered.

I recommend *Cranes are Flying* and *Wings* if you haven't seen them. The maturity the USSR was dealing with women issues in film is incredible compared to the states where women were still nothing more than a commodity at the time.

https://youtu.be/8V7NHxgpGMU?si=42zDKNcuq3PhcfS_

https://youtu.be/yY_GXobuXdg?si=AgEH6Ywk8HmGmnxp

(If anyone enjoys making fan trailers, wings 1966 could really use a better one)

Yes, you perfectly describe what I found intriguing about the movie. The “Judas” character wanting to live for livings sake, despite the conditions of living going against the values of his soul (working with the Nazis). Very very interesting. I think it calls to challenge the meaning of death as well. 

There’s also the scene where his sickly friend is being hung in front of the village, and his looks at a young boy who is crying. He gives the boy a slight smile, as if being happy to die. I think that goes beyond patriotism, but also being content with dying for what you believe in. Very powerful. 

And yes! That mosin scene - I swear there’s another movie that shows something similar? Can’t remember. 

Wings! I haven’t watched since I was a teenager, definitely needs a rewatch.

Thanks for the recommendations :)
I don’t know! I wanna say I think it was?
You're making me want to rewatch it now.

I honestly think it’s worth it, I think the movie holds up quite well. 

I think I’m gonna rewatch it already! Hahaha

I highly recommend Larisa Shepitko’s earlier film Wings (1966) as well. The movie is about a woman who was a pilot during WWII but is now a dean of a military school 20 years later. She’s dissatisfied with her life and having trouble finding her place after the war. The movie engages with the war from different angles that I had never seen which is one of the aspects that I think has made a lasting impression. It also has one of the most striking endings I’ve ever seen which I personally think is extremely overlooked/under seen. The cherry on top is it’s like less than 85 minutes and on criterion channel.
I agree it's a fantastic film as are *The Cranes are Flying* as well as Wings. Just wanted to leave a recommendation for *The 41st* and *Letter Never Sent* as well.

Please take the time and watch the 5 part mini series called "The unknown Soldier" from 2017. its a Finnish movie originally called "Tuntematon sotilas"

based off a book and a movie from 1955

It follows a Finnish company during the continuation war in the fight against the soviets. 

There are different cuts, a 3.5 ish movie cut and then a 5 part 1 ish hour mini series and i cant recommend it more .

i believe that it is one of the best WW2 based war movie/shows.

one day i will do a proper breakdown of the objectively reasons why i think its the best, but that day is not today.

you are just going to have to "trust me bro" for now

I have watched almost all of the greatest (and worst) war movies and shows and for me this takes the cake.
